situation:
You are to assume the role of operations coordinator at CLAYBOURNE ARTS CENTER, a nonprofit theater and gallery that has served its city for thirty years. The executive director (judge) has asked you to recommend how the center should answer a second straight season of falling ticket sales.

TIDEWATER STAGE COLLECTIVE opened two seasons ago and has taken a growing share of the same audience. Tidewater sells seats cheaply when a run opens and raises the price as a night fills, and Claybourne's box office staff have asked to adopt the same approach. None of them has ever run a pricing system that moves.

Claybourne's name is known in the city for one thing: a seat any family can afford. Demand-based pricing on sold-out nights would raise revenue, and it would also price out the community audience that name is built on, while the staff would need training the center has never given.

GRANDVIEW MUTUAL BANK has offered a season sponsorship large enough to close the gap without a price change. Accepting the sponsorship would give the bank approval over the titles Claybourne programs, surrendering control the artistic staff hold now. The executive director (judge) wants your recommendation on which course the center takes. The executive director (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of the executive director at CLAYBOURNE ARTS CENTER. Business background is the same as the situation above. You have asked the participant to recommend how the center answers a second straight season of falling ticket sales, and what that choice protects and what it gives up.

The participant will present their recommendation to you in a role-play to take place in your office. You will begin the role-play by greeting the participant and asking to hear their ideas.

During the role-play, you are to ask the following questions of the participant:
judgeQuestions: How would you explain this to the box office staff who asked for the change?
What would you say to a family that can no longer afford a seat?
